claims.text: In-situ aberration-corrected TEM with a heating stage can reveal atomic-scale restructuring in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles during heating.
Observing restructuring during heating can provide insight into the thermal stability of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The proposed nanoparticles have an equiatomic or near-equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt composition.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are assumed to have a disordered structure at room temperature.
Incremental heating in an aberration-corrected TEM enables real-time imaging of atomic-scale changes during a temperature ramp.
Controlled heating rates can help avoid beam-induced artifacts.
Surface diffusion, grain-boundary migration, and phase transitions can be detected through changes in lattice contrast and spacing.
Increasing temperature enhances atomic motion and can cause surface diffusion.
Increasing temperature may induce ordering transitions in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Thermally induced atomic rearrangements should appear as changes in lattice fringes and contrast in high-resolution TEM images.
Phase transitions or surface restructuring should occur at temperatures theoretically associated with changes in thermal stability.
Room-temperature TEM would show a homogeneous, disordered atomic structure characteristic of nearly equiatomic high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Electron-beam damage and reduced high-temperature resolution may influence the observations.
TEM observations of these nanoparticles may not capture bulk effects when behavior is dominated by surface phenomena.
